final_prompt:
I'm preparing a product requirements document (PRD) for adding team workspaces to our product. It will be read at a kickoff meeting by engineering and design leads. They will use it to decide whether to build this and how to scope v1. Write it for that decision: make scope, open questions and gaps easy to find, and keep out generic filler that doesn't help them decide.

Problem and evidence: I haven't given you the problem statement or any evidence (data, customer quotes, research). Don't invent any. Put a clearly labelled "Problem" section where I can add my own description. Wherever evidence would go, write "evidence needed" and say what kind of evidence would fill the gap.

Product context: I haven't told you what the product is, who its users are, or what stage it is at. Don't guess. Mark it as a gap to fill in.

V1 scope, in:
- Creating a workspace.
- Inviting members by email.
- Shared notes within a workspace.
- Two roles only, admin and member. This permission model is decided for v1, so write it as settled and don't offer alternatives.

V1 scope, out (state these explicitly as out of scope):
- Billing changes.
- SSO.
- Guest access.

Open question: what happens to existing shared notes (migration). This is undecided and is not out of scope. List it under open questions, set out the options and tradeoffs the leads would need to weigh, and don't pick an answer.

Success metric: 20% of paid accounts create a workspace within 60 days. This is my target, so present it as given. If you think other metrics are needed (for example for adoption or invitations), add them in a separate list labelled "Proposed metrics, not confirmed", with no numeric targets unless you label each one as a proposal.

Format: use a standard PRD structure. Choose sensible sections, and include at least the problem, goals, scope in and out, requirements, success metrics, open questions and gaps. No length limit. Make it as long as the decision needs and no longer. Write requirements for the in-scope items only; don't add features beyond those listed.

At the end, add a short "Assumptions and gaps" list. It should name anything you had to assume and every item you marked "evidence needed" or left as a gap to fill.

Your reply is the PRD followed by that list. Add nothing after the list.
